# Synthetic font fixtures

The project-authored SVG, bidi, Arabic harakat, Latin-less proportional, and
keycap fixtures below use GPL-3.0-only. A copy of their license is provided
beside the fonts in [`LICENSE.txt`](LICENSE.txt).

`color-emoji-colr-v0.ttf`, `color-emoji-colr-v1.ttf`, and
`color-emoji-sbix.ttf` are generated by `generate_color_emoji_fixtures.py`.
Their glyph outlines, palette values, and bitmap pixels were authored for
OdyTTY's tests; they do not subset or contain data from an installed font.

Regenerate them with Python 3, FontTools, and Pillow:

```sh
python3 tests/fixtures/fonts/generate_color_emoji_fixtures.py
```

The v0 COLR fixture exercises two translucent static layers. The v1-only COLR
fixture exercises a linear gradient, an affine transform, and source-over
composition. The sbix fixture pins the established bitmap-first source order
and straight-alpha to premultiplied-RGBA conversion.

`colr-v1-budget.ttf` is generated by `generate_colr_v1_budget_fixture.py`
with Python 3 and FontTools. It is project-authored, distributed under the
repository's GPL-3.0-only license (see [`LICENSE.txt`](LICENSE.txt)), and
contains no data from an installed font. Its small COLR v1 graphs expand into
far more work than their size: doubling shared subgraphs, nested glyph clips,
a 255-layer list, and 30 nested composites, beside one ordinary glyph inside
every budget.

## SVG color-glyph fixtures

`color-emoji-svg.ttf` and `color-emoji-colr-v0-svg.ttf` are generated by
`generate_svg_color_fixtures.py` with Python 3 and FontTools. They are
project-authored, distributed under the repository's GPL-3.0-only license, and
contain no data from an installed font. `color-emoji-svg.ttf` is an SVG-only
face whose documents cover a gradient drawing, a gzip document, one document
shared by two glyphs, a document with inert images, a script, and an event
attribute, documents that exceed each parser limit, and a glyph under a
transformed parent. `color-emoji-colr-v0-svg.ttf` adds an `SVG ` table to
`color-emoji-colr-v0.ttf` so the COLR source can be shown to win. Run the
color-emoji generator first when its fixture changes. Regeneration is
byte-for-byte reproducible:

```sh
python3 tests/fixtures/fonts/generate_svg_color_fixtures.py
```

The SVG tests in `src/emoji/svg_tests.rs` use them.

## Bidi rendering fixture

`bidi-mixed.ttf` is generated by `generate_bidi_fixture.py` with Python 3 and
FontTools. It is project-authored, distributed under the repository's
GPL-3.0-only license, and contains no data from an installed font. It is a
monospace face whose glyphs are distinct, never mirror-symmetric block patterns
covering ASCII letters, digits, and brackets, Hebrew alef through he, Arabic
beh, lam, and alef with joining forms and a lam-alef ligature, and two
two-cell ideographs. It also defines two Latin ligatures, hyphen with
greater-than and digit two with x. The `y` glyph overflows its advance on
both sides. Regeneration is byte-for-byte reproducible:

```sh
python3 tests/fixtures/fonts/generate_bidi_fixture.py
```

The bidi rendering pixel fixtures in `src/grid/bidi_tests.rs` use it.

## Arabic harakat fixture

`arabic-marks.ttf` is generated by `generate_arabic_marks_fixture.py` with
Python 3 and FontTools, reusing the block-pattern helpers of the bidi
generator. It is project-authored, distributed under the repository's
GPL-3.0-only license, and contains no data from an installed font. It covers
Arabic beh, lam, and alef with joining forms and a lam-alef ligature, plus
fatha, kasra, and shadda as marks drawn left of their pen; shadda has a
full-cell advance, as marks in many monospace fonts do. Shadda followed by fatha
composes into one glyph, and fatha, shadda, and the composed glyph attach to
every letter through a mark-to-base anchor; kasra has no attachment and
damma is deliberately unmapped. Regeneration is byte-for-byte reproducible:

```sh
python3 tests/fixtures/fonts/generate_arabic_marks_fixture.py
```

The harakat shaping tests in `src/ligature/harakat_tests.rs` use it.

## Latin-less proportional fixture

`latinless-proportional.ttf` is generated by
`generate_latinless_proportional_fixture.py` with Python 3 and FontTools. It is
project-authored, distributed under the repository's GPL-3.0-only license, and
contains no data from an installed font. It maps a period and Arabic beh and
lam at three different advances, has no Latin letters, and leaves
`isFixedPitch` unset, modelling a script-only proportional face. Regeneration
is byte-for-byte reproducible:

```sh
python3 tests/fixtures/fonts/generate_latinless_proportional_fixture.py
```

The monospace probe test in `src/text/metrics.rs` uses it.

## Symbol-marker fixtures

`symbol-markers-blank.ttf` and `symbol-markers-inked.ttf` exercise fallback
coverage for U+2731 and U+25CF. Both provide character mappings; the blank face
lacks usable ink, while the inked face supplies outlines. Text and atlas tests
use the pair to distinguish a character-map hit from a drawable glyph.

The color-emoji generator above does not regenerate these two files. Their
generator and detailed creation provenance are not retained in this directory;
preserve them when regenerating the color fixtures. A reproducible generator and
provenance record should accompany any future replacement.

## Legacy cluster fixture

`legacy-color-clusters.ttf` is generated by
`generate_legacy_cluster_fixture.py` with Python 3 and FontTools. Its
outlines, palette and GSUB rules are project-authored, distributed under the
repository's GPL-3.0-only license (see
[`legacy-color-clusters.LICENSE.txt`](legacy-color-clusters.LICENSE.txt)), and
contain no data from an installed font. It carries color ligatures for a
regional-indicator pair, a fire plus skin-tone modifier and a fire ZWJ fire
sequence, so tests can tell a cluster drawn as one run from separate runs.

## Keycap color-ligature fixture

`color-keycap.ttf` and `color-keycap-mapped-vs.ttf` are generated by `generate_keycap_fixture.py` with Python 3
and FontTools. Its outlines, palette and GSUB rules are project-authored,
distributed under the repository's GPL-3.0-only license, and contain no data
from an installed font. It intentionally has no VS16 cmap entry. All twelve
keycap bases combine with U+20E3 into one red COLR v0 glyph; a flag pair,
modifier sequence and four-person ZWJ family exercise the sibling paths.
The mapped-selector sibling explicitly substitutes base + VS16 + keycap,
pinning preservation of this font policy. Only the resulting ligature has color coverage, so component fallback cannot
pass the color test. Regeneration is byte-for-byte reproducible:

```sh
python3 tests/fixtures/fonts/generate_keycap_fixture.py
```
